clusters.name: Monitorability as a monitor's ability to predict a target property
clusters.description: Monitorability is a relation between what a model exposes and a reader: the degree to which a given monitor can predict a specified property of the model's behaviour, without requiring the CoT to reproduce the model's internal computation.

clusters.name: Scoring monitorability: metrics and evaluation designs
clusters.description: Monitorability is operationalized as the agreement between a monitor's verdict and a ground-truth label for the target property, summarized by a statistic such as g-mean², AUROC or binned MSE, with the label produced by an intervention, a known solution process or a verifiable outcome.

clusters.name: Monitorability as faithful and complete verbalization
clusters.description: Monitorability is a property of the trace itself: the CoT must state, faithfully and in some versions completely, the factors and steps that produced the answer, so that monitoring presupposes faithfulness.

clusters.name: Necessity and causal dependence of the CoT
clusters.description: The condition under which a CoT is expected to be monitorable: the task cannot be solved without the CoT (necessity), or the answer causally depends on what the CoT says (load-bearing reasoning).

clusters.name: Legibility and coverage: a reader can follow, check or reconstruct the reasoning
clusters.description: The CoT must be readable by a specified reader (a human, a weaker model or the monitor) and must carry enough of the reasoning for that reader to check the answer or reach it; the failure is illegibility, language drift or missing steps.

clusters.name: Encoded reasoning and steganography
clusters.description: The CoT carries information that the model uses but that a reader cannot recover, because it is hidden in word choice, syntax or reasoning patterns; definitions differ on whether the reader it is hidden from is a human or the monitor.

clusters.name: Obfuscation, evasion and controllability
clusters.description: The misbehaviour continues while the trace stops revealing it to the monitor, through omission, misleading framing, changed internal representations or deliberate control of the CoT, usually as a result of optimization pressure or monitor awareness.

clusters.name: Monitors, monitor scopes and oversight channels
clusters.description: Companion definitions of the reader: what a CoT monitor is, what it observes (CoT, actions, activations, summaries), how protocols chain monitors, and channels in which the model reports on itself.

clusters.name: Monitorability and legibility taxes
clusters.description: The cost paid to keep reasoning monitorable or legible, variously the capability forgone by not optimizing the CoT, by using a smaller model at higher reasoning effort, by compressing the trace, or by training for checkability.

mismatches.finding: Confirmed mismatch. Attributed to Korbak et al. 2025 (with Baker et al. 2025): monitoring is useful only if the reasoning reflects what drives the answers. Korbak never states it and states the opposite: 'CoT does not need to completely represent the actual reasoning process in order to be a valuable additional safety layer' (§1). Nearest: the externalized reasoning property, which 'does not guarantee monitorability'.

Confirmed mismatch. Monitorable glossed as 'its CoT faithfully externalizes reasoning', attributed to Korbak et al. 2025; Korbak gives no definition of monitorability and says the CoT need not completely represent the reasoning process. Baker et al. 2025 supports only faithfulness with respect to the monitored property (partial).

Confirmed mismatch for Korbak et al. 2025 and Emmons et al. 2025 (necessity): neither requires the CoT to 'faithfully reflect the model's internal decision-making path'; Korbak states the opposite, Emmons argues for monitorability instead of faithfulness. Chen et al. 2025, also cited, does state the requirement; Baker et al. 2025 partial (faithfulness w.r.t. the monitored property only).

Partially supported. 'Faithfulness is a prerequisite for CoT monitorability' holds in Baker only for faithfulness redefined as a sufficient statistic for the monitored property v (§5.1); Baker says monitorability, 'and not faithfulness in isolation', is what matters. Occhipinti's faithfulness is hint mention plus dependence.

Partially supported. Baker decouples monitorability from faithfulness as representing the reasoning process, but still requires the latent to be faithful with respect to the monitored property v ('If a monitor M can accurately predict property v from latent z, then z must be faithful with respect to v'), so 'independent of the model's true reasoning process' overstates it.

Confirmed mismatch. Attributed to Meek et al. 2025: reasoning can be monitorable without being faithful. Meek reports the reverse divergence ('models can appear faithful yet remain hard to monitor when they leave out key factors') and includes faithfulness as half of its monitorability score.

Confirmed mismatch. The legibility/coverage autorater is attributed to Emmons et al. 2025 'When chain of thought is necessary...', which never uses 'coverage'; the rubric is in emmons2025pragmatic (A Pragmatic Way to Measure CoT Monitorability).

Confirmed mismatch. 'The hint experiment setting [15]' with [15] = Lanham et al. 2023; Lanham contains no hint experiments ('We intervene on the CoT produced by the model rather than few shot prompt examples'). Nearest: its description of Turpin et al. 2023's biasing few-shot examples; the setting is Turpin 2023 / Chen 2025.

Confirmed for Guan: Guan never defines verifiability of a reasoning trace; 'verifiable' occurs once, for answers ('easily verifiable answers'). Nearest: the process archetype. Co-cited Chan et al. 2025 is not in the map (not settled).

Term misattributed: 'default' never occurs in Guan; 'default monitorability' is Emmons et al. 2025 (pragmatic)'s term. Guan does supply the robustness-under-optimization side (runs that explicitly reward CoT obfuscation).

Partially supported. Lanham never mentions monitoring; Turpin mentions it once generically. Chen et al. 2025 does tie faithfulness evaluation to monitoring; the 'proxy for monitorability' framing is Chen's and Korbak's.
Not settled. Compressed reasoning patterns attributed to Baker et al. 2025; no Baker record and 'compress' does not occur in its text; figures not inspected.
Not settled. 'Covert misbehavior' attributed to Schoen et al. 2025, whose text speaks of 'covert action rates'; no record for the term.
Not settled. Reference [6] resolves to Greenblatt et al. 2024 (not in the map); the extraction note says the work described is Roger & Greenblatt 2023.

Not settled. 'Non-intentional' obfuscation: Drori's spillover is unintended, but Guan rewards obfuscation deliberately (while also mentioning accidental CoT pressure) and Haskins induces it via documents about monitoring.
